findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: REPEAT Inspector observed the cook line sanitizer bucket to have < 100 PPM of quat sanitizer. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated the sanitizer was made early this morning and immediately switched it out with a fresh bucket measuring 200 PPM. Ensure sanitizer concentration is checked regularly to maintain sanitization in facility.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
REPEAT Inspector observed two areas in need of re-caulking

1. The caulk attaching the triple sink to the wall is cracking and in need of replacement. There are soils present in the caulk as well. Discussed with PIC. Ensure caulk is replaced to create a smooth, non absorbent, and easily cleanable surface.

2. The caulk attaching the mop sink to the wall was observed to have a build up of soils and be cracking as well. Discussed with PIC. Ensure caulk is replaced to create a smooth, non absorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket was observed to have a concentration of 100 ppm (q).  Discuss with PIC, corrected on-site.  Ensure sanitizer buckets are changed more often to maintain the proper sanitizing concentration of 200 ppm.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
The hand sink by the walk-in cooler drips from the faucet.  Ensure the faucet is repaired and maintained in good working order.

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The fan grates in the walk-in cooler were observed to contain an accumulation of dust.  Periodic cleaning of the fan grates is necessary to prevent dust accumulation and food contamination.  Ensure grates are cleaned regularly.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. 

Staff members present are unable to provide pertinent paperwork to the inspector regarding employee illness, certificates for staff, Norovirus cleanup, pest control, etc. See that all staff are aware of where these documents are located and are able to provide them to inspector upon request.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Neither employee present today has a certified food manager’s certificate. See that enough staff have taken the 8-hour course to cover hours of operation appropriately.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Staff employee health reporting agreements not available to inspector for review. See that staff keep this documentation on file and ensure staff are knowledgeable of their reporting responsibilities.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

Norovirus cleanup policy not available for inspector to review. See #1. Will follow up.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Sanitizer not available for staff upon inspector arrival. According to staff, a sanitizer bucket has not been in use all day today. Discussed with PIC. See that a sanitizer bucket is available during all hours of operation, changed as needed or at least every 4 hours. COS- PIC made a new sanitizer bucket.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. 

Neither staff member on duty has a food handler card. See that all staff, with the exception of certified food managers, obtain a food handler’s card. Keep copies on hand for inspector review.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
3-201.11: (A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source and not from private home. (P)
There is an unfinished, vacant unit to this facility next door. The unit is owned by the same person, therefore Domino's has been using it as a dry storage area for excess soda, pizza boxes, and cornmeal. The vacant unit is not a permitted site, has not had a plan review as a food service facility, and has not been subject to inspection by SCDPH, lacks important items such as sealed/finished walls, door sweep to external door, etc.Therefore, food stored here is considered "not from an approved source". Discussed with PIC at time of inspection. The facility must remove excess dry goods from the vacant unit immediately and store back into permitted Domino's by the follow up date. If the facility wishes to utilize the vacant unit for storage, they must obtain a plan review, permit, and inspection prior to doing so.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers. 

See violation 11. Inside vacant unit, there is a visibly soiled container of cornmeal (used for dough). There are small (dead) flies present inside the cornmeal and the outside of the container contains dirt and other debris. Discussed with PIC. Cornmeal was voluntarily discarded by PIC at time of inspection. Food may not be stored in the vacant unit because it lacks proper protection from contamination, and it is not continuously monitored for contamination conditions.

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment:
5-501.15: (A) Receptacles for REFUSE used outside shall be designed and constructed to have tight-fitting lids, doors, or covers. (B) Receptacles for REFUSE shall be installed so debris and insect and rodent attraction are minimized. 
5-501.115: A storage area and enclosure for REFUSE, recyclables, or returnables shall be maintained free of unnecessary items, as specified under § 6-501.114, and clean. 

Dumpster for facility is broken, missing a lid, and is placed outside the brick cubicle. Debris is observed strewn about inside brick cubicle. Discussed with PIC. Waste haulers are responsible for emptying the dumpsters, however facility is responsible for maintaining sound condition of storage areas surrounding dumpsters. This may be a potential harborage situation for pests later on. Ensure employees maintain this area free of debris.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15  (C) Exterior door allows access for pests. Exterior doors shall be: 1) self-closing, 2) solid and tight fitting, 3) limited to designed use. 

Noted at the preopening, exterior door behind the restaurant needed sealed on the bottom with door sweep. Observed at inspection today that a door sweep has still not be installed. Inspector will follow up to ensure door sweep has been installed.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14  (Pf) Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic. 

Quat sanitizer test strips not presented at time of inspection. Provide test strips for quaternary sanitizer (and bleach) by follow up date.
